transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

Since the crash, even small things on the road make me jump out of my skin, and I can’t bring myself to drive like I used to. My daughter finally convinced me to come in because it's gotten so hard to get around.
Since the crash, do you also have unwanted memories or nightmares about it, or try to avoid thoughts, places, or reminders of the accident?

Yes, if I hear a siren or see a speeding car on TV, I'm right back in that intersection hearing the metal crunch and my wife screaming. I also do everything I can to avoid the highway or the spot where we got hit, sticking only to local back roads because just thinking about those places makes my chest tight.
Since the crash, have you been feeling constantly on edge or more irritable, having trouble sleeping, or being easily startled by sudden noises or movements?

Yes, I lie awake for hours replaying things and wake up constantly, which leaves me so exhausted that I've been snapping at my wife and daughter over little things. When I'm in the car, I'm constantly scanning the road on edge, and any sudden noise like a horn makes my whole body jerk and leaves my hands shaking.
How long have these symptoms been going on since the crash? Have they lasted for more than one month?

Yes, they've been going on ever since the accident, which was about a year and a half ago—specifically, a year and seven months. They really haven't let up at all in all this time, so it's been much longer than a month.
Have these symptoms been causing problems in your daily life, like work, relationships, or driving, and are they still happening now?

Yes, they are still happening every day, and it has completely disrupted my life. I've had to cut back on my library volunteering and even skipped my grandchild's school play because of the driving involved. On top of that, I'm just too exhausted and on edge to manage the house or care for my wife the way I used to.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets criteria for post-traumatic stress disorder following a motor vehicle crash, with exposure to a qualifying traumatic event, intrusive re-experiencing (distressing memories triggered by sirens/TV, nightmares implied by replaying and sleep disruption), marked avoidance of trauma reminders (highway, crash site), persistent hyperarousal (hypervigilance, exaggerated startle, insomnia, irritability), duration well beyond 1 month, and clear functional impairment in driving, volunteering, family life, and daily responsibilities.
